یا سکانس دیگه پلیس میاد دختره بیدار میشه وحشت میکنه و فیلمساز با کلوزآپ از چهره ی پلیس زور میزنه بترسونه ولی بیشتر خنده داره واقعا، حالا این پلیسه تو فیلم چیکار داره رو بیخیال.(ژانر وحشت بهترین راه برای ساخت یه فیلم دری وری که توش هر چی میخوای بزاری، ظاهرا خود هیچکاک از پلیس میترسه و اینجا پلیس آورده که ماهم بترسیم!) یکی از مسخره ترین و مزخرف ترین صحنه های فیلم هم اونجایی که باران میاد، و صدای آدامای دیگه رو برای زن پخش میشه که ظاهرا تصورات ذهنی خود زنه. واقعا فاجعه ست تا این حد عاجز ! بعد به اینم تازه میگن تعلیق! باران میاد زنه تو تصوارتش صدا آدمای پشت سرشو میشنوه چند باری هم به پشت سر نگاه میکنه و موسیقی ؛ این اضطراب و تعلیق اسمش. و اما برسیم به سکانس بشدت پر سروصدا و معروف و البته خنده دار حمام. یه سیاهی از پشت میاد، پرده رو میکشه و همراه با موسیقی چاقو رو این ور اون ور میکنه، زنه یه جیغ واضحات مصنوعی و صدای اصابت چاقو. به این میگن قتل؟؟ خیلی جدی اینجوری قتل میسازن. چرا به این صحنه ی احمقانه میگن یکی از بهترین لحظات ترسناک سینما؟؟ شاید چون بیش از ۷۰ دورین استفاده شده، یا شایدم چون برای صدای ضربه از خربزه و برای خون هم شکلات استفاده شده ما باید بگیم ترسناک،  اضطراب تعلیق ولی در واقع هیچی نیست، جز یه سکانس مزخرف خنده دار و طنز! چندین بار هم سریع سریع کات میکنه که صرفا هیجانی کنه. مجموعا فیلمساز اصلا بلد نیست یه قتل ساده بسازه. نما هایی که از قصر نشون میده هم واقعا جوکه، شبیه خانه ی ارواح تو انیمیشن هاست، انگار هیچکاک میخواد بچه بترسونه . سکانس کشتن کارآگاه هم همین طوره ارزش بحث نداره. اونجایی هم که خواهره میره به سمت قصر، چندین بار کات میزنه دختر و در قصر که داره نزدیک میشه بهش، باز زور میزنه ترسناک نشونش بده، بشدت ضعیف و مسخره! بعد میره پیر زن رو پیدا میکنه زن برمیگرده و صورت استخونی اش رو میبینیم و بازم جیغ و موسیقی و تلاش فیلمساز که بتونه یه لحظه مخاطب رو بترسونه. یه نکته هم راجب این سکانس بگم، جمجمه پیرزن خیلی فیکه حالا اینو از هیچکاک میگیریم ولی واکنش دختر و جیغ زدن هاش از اون هم فیک تر و تا حدودی خنده داره. بعد پایان فیلم هم یه نفر میاد و مجری وار تعریف میکنه،  که این فلان بود و... ظاهرا فیلمساز میخواسته آخر فیلم رو جمع و جور کنه که ملت نگن چرا فیلم رو نفهمیدیم، اولا این که میایی تار و پود فیلم رو باز میکنی خودش بده بعد تازه با دیالوگ های یه شخصیتی که تازه تو فیلم ظاهر شده دیگه بدتر! در مجموع سایکو فیلم عقیم و پرمدعایی هست که فقط تلاش میکنه با بازی های تصنعی، نماهای مختلف از قصر و چهره ی نورمن، موسیقی و... مخاطب رو حداقل برای یکبار بترسونه ولی حتی در همین کار ساده هم موفق نمیشه و بجاش یه فیلم مفتضح و خنده دار تحویل میده و بی شک یکی از عقب افتاده ترین و مزخرف ترین آثار هیچکاک. هیچکاک کلا یه فیلم متوسط داره به اسم پنجره پشتی که بدک نیست وگرنه که کلا آدم بدرد بخوری برای سینما نیست.

Honestly, I did not really like Psycho. I thought the movie was slow, and it was hard for me to stay interested. I understand why it is considered an important horror movie, but it just wasn’t my type of film. Norman Bates was an interesting character, and the ending was unexpected, but overall, I didn’t enjoy watching it. One filmmaking choice I noticed was the editing in the famous shower scene. The quick cuts between camera angles made the scene feel intense and shocking. The music also helped create suspense and made the audience feel uncomfortable. Before taking Film Arts, I probably wouldn’t have noticed how much editing and music can change the feeling of a scene. I connected Psycho to Halloween because both movies use suspense, creepy music, and a mysterious killer. Even though I liked Halloween more, I can understand how Psycho helped influence horror movies.

Psycho changes how movies build and deliver scary moments instead of using a monster he makeit feel like they are peeking into private moments alongside the characters.The movie works so well because it does not rely on jump scares, building tension through camera angles, and a twist in the middle of the story. . The story is on a conflict around secrets, guilt, and double lives. Crane makes a decision to steal $40,000 setting off her journey. Just as she decides to return the money and fix her mistake, her story ends not good ,and the focus shifts to bates and his broken mind. Norman’s highlights the main ideas about being trapped by the past which is shown through the stuffed birds sitting around his office. The dead frozen birds represent how Norman is stuck and controlled by his mother's memory. By setting the story at an empty motel the film shows how guilt can trap a person leaving viewers with a weird ending. Hitchcock uses filming and editing choices to make the motel feel unsettling. He uses black and white lighting with deep shadows to show norman’s two sides and he shoots through doorways to make the viewer feel like they are seeing things they shouldn't see. The best scene is the shower attack where the editing speeds up creating a chaotic sequence without showing blood. The editor cuts from the soap suds in the drain straight to a close up shot of marion’s eye. Psycho stand out is how it takes away the main character halfway through leaving the audience with the killer. Every choice keeps you focused on what will happen next, earning it a clear 2 out of 5 stars. It connects directly to Se7en, another movie that skips happy endings and uses rainy, cramped settings to look at the dark side of human behavior. While Se7en is a modern detective story psycho is the exact style decades earlier by proving a scary movie is built in the editing room.

04/10. Falando em termos fotográficos, achei o filme muito lindo. Sou a favor de filmes com boa fotografia e ambientação. O filme entra, para mim, no famoso "Vale da Estranheza", principalmente o personagem Norman Bates. Ao assistir, você sente realmente que o personagem de Bates é alguém extremamente estranho, mas ao mesmo tempo normal, o que é inexplicavelmente cativante. Falando em termos de roteiro, achei a primeira metade do filme confusa, a segunda metade sobre a investigação foi mais interessante, apesar do plot da mãe de Bates ser de certa forma previsível, falando agora nos termos cinematográficos do século 21, claro. Para mim, o filme é superestimado, é um clássico sem dúvidas e que revolucionou a indústria cinematográfica, mas pela expectativa colocada, achei que seria realmente mais impactante. Finalizando, o filme tem seu charme, tem seus pontos positivos, mas achei um filme simples, enxuto e de certa forma inconclusivo, pois senti que ficou alguns pontos em aberto.

Hoo boy... I... uh. Hmm. Thought this was quite shit? I know it doesn't help that it's been memed and parodied and spoiled to hell in the last 60 years so there were few surprises for me in 2026, but how this ended up with so much more cultural cache than my other excellent horror watch today ( The Innocents , released just a year later) truly escapes me. Although maybe it says something that we're generally more amped for a morally suspect lady getting stabbed a bunch by a queer coded villain under the gaze of a gleeful director (with more than a little sense of "hey maybe she deserved it?" messaging - bleugh), than we are hyped for something more complex about women in caregiving roles and their relationships to their charges. Makes a certain kind of bleak sense. Cinematography fairly faultless for the most part, although even there I found segments that looked for all the world like it was being filmed in a multi-cam studio. Hitchcock’s sacred cow is one of the most overrated films I’ve seen to date. As it is with other movies, age and influence doesn’t automatically make something good. Was Hitler a good person because he was influential? Well I guess that’s up for you to decide. Psycho is an excellent example of something old and influential being critically undeserving of praise. The movie is a dragged out snooze fest. Nothing happens for long stretches of time as characters drive around and talk in circles. The pacing is slow for what is supposed to be a thriller, and as someone who is usually patient with movies, I can honestly say I spent most of this film waiting for anything to happen. It never did. Most of the movie is also served as a frame for the uneventful driving scenes. They’re really just abstractions that amount to nothing. The kills are genuinely horrid. The famous shower scene is a masterclass in editing and the power of suggestion, sure, but the killing itself is clumsy, bloodless, and almost laughable compared to the murder scenes we see in our movies today (and even other movies from the mid-1960s). And the other murders in the film? Even worse. Awkward staging, zero impact, zero tension. People act like these are the gold standard of cinematic murder; they’re not. They’re dated and ineffective. Acting is mostly mediocre, and Perkins’ performance as Norman is the only real bright spot. The rest of the cast is stuck in stiff, theatrical mid-century mode. Janet Leigh is okay until she’s gone. Everyone else feels like they’re doing a radio play. The dialogue doesn’t help either; lots of awkward exposition and stilted exchanges that kill any momentum. And the big twist that is supposedly one of the greatest of all time? It’s not some genius revelation. Once you see it coming (or even if you don’t), it lands with a thud. Hitchcock spends the entire movie developing a mystery just to flatten it with a lecture, and it’s not clever, it’s clunky. We can all appreciate that this movie invented a ton of ideas that would go on to define Hollywood, but are we rating this based on influence? No, we’re rating on how good this particular film is, not the other films it influenced. Influence isn’t the same as quality. Plenty of later films took the basic ideas and executed them better, tighter, and with actual tension. People give Psycho a free pass for being first. That and Hitchcock’s clever use of the tricks he learned filming within the constraints of the low budget and the Production Code.  Those are interesting footnotes, they do not make the movie itself good or entertaining. Boring, overpraised, and held up as a masterpiece mostly because critics and cinephiles refuse to admit that “classic” and “actually gripping” aren’t synonyms.

Psycho Film Review Psycho was a good movie overall, but I felt like the pacing was too slow during the beginning. As the movie progressed, especially after the first murder, I became much more interested in the story. My favorite parts of the film were its cinematography and musical score, which helped create suspense and made certain scenes memorable. Norman Bates' character development throughout the film is what grasped my attention more than any of the other characters. At first glance, he appeared to be an innocent, shy, and modest person. However, his demeanor changed when Marion Crane suggested that he put his mother in a nursing home. Not long afterward, Marion was murdered, which changed the direction of the story and made the movie more engaging. Her disappearance caused her sister, Lila Crane, Detective Milton Arbogast, and Sam Loomis to investigate what happened to her. As the investigation continued, Norman murdered more people, including Arbogast. This led Lila and Sam to investigate the Bates Motel themselves. Eventually, Lila discovered that Norman's mother had been dead for years and that Norman had been disguising himself as her when committing the murders. The final revelation was one of the most interesting parts of the movie because it explained Norman's strange behavior and his disturbing relationship with his mother. The musical score in Psycho is what helped build suspense throughout the film, especially during the shower scene when Marion Crane was murdered. The violins were the most notable part of the musical score. The use of screeching violins made the movie eerier and created an unsettling atmosphere. There is also a leitmotif in the film that helps associate music with Norman Bates and creates a sense of suspense whenever danger seems to be approaching. I also appreciated the editing in this film. I noticed that the editors used dissolve transitions and fades to black. I also noticed the rapid cuts during the shower scene, which made it feel more intense and chaotic. The film Psycho helped open my eyes to movies that were created in the 1960s.  The musical score in this film is unique compared to other films. I haven't seen any other movies where they use violins in their musical scores. I loved certain aspects of this movie, one of them being how the film kicked off after the first murder. One of the aspects that I didn't like about this film is how it started off slowly. The dialogue between the characters and the overall events leading up to the first murder wasn't the best in my opinion. Overall, I would rate this movie a 3 out of 5 stars. I would compare and contrast this move to Catch Me If You Can, which is my top 15 favorite movies of all time. The comparisons that I noticed are how identity was used in both movies. Bates was taking the identity of his mom, and Frank Abagnale Jr. took identities of multiple people throughout the movie. I also found both movies did a good job of choosing actors that did a good job of portraying Bates and Abagnale. Catch Me If You Can had color and is a more recent movie, while Psycho is an older movie with no color. Psycho has a slower pace at the beginning of the film while Catch Me If You Can has a more interesting beginning in my opinion.

I thought Psycho was a good movie because it kept me guessing and had some unexpected moments. The biggest surprise was when Marion died because I thought she was going to be the main character for the whole movie. After that scene, the story changed, and I became more interested in finding out what was going on with Norman Bates. I liked how the movie built suspense without needing a lot of action. It was different from most movies I watch, but it still kept me interested. One of the main themes in Psycho is that people are not always who they seem to be. Norman seems like a quiet and normal guy when Marion first meets him, but later we learn that he is hiding a lot. The scene where Norman watches Marion through a hole in the wall shows that there is something wrong with him. The Bates house also adds to the mystery because it looks dark and creepy. The movie keeps the audience guessing about Norman and his mother until the truth finally comes out. The cinematography, editing, and music helped make the movie scary. One scene that stood out to me was when Marion gets attacked in the shower. The quick cuts between Marion, the shower curtain, and the attacker make the scene feel chaotic. The high pitched violin music makes it even more intense. I thought this scene was effective because the editing and sound made it scary without showing everything directly. The movie also uses black-and-white shots and shadows to create a creepy atmosphere. Overall, I would give Psycho 3 out of 5 stars. I can see why people like it because it has a surprising story and builds suspense, but horror and suspense movies are not really my type. I prefer movies with more action, like Land of Bad, which is my number one movie. While Psycho focuses more on mystery and making the audience guess what will happen, Land of Bad has more action and intense moments. I thought Psycho was interesting, but it is not the kind of movie I would normally choose to watch.
